- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment is volatile — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for the first 3–5 days if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values (neutral or negative), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast to trigger correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates in the final 5–7 days — especially if sentiment is bullish — apply a 1–2% downward taper toward end of horizon.
